cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a carved wooden two-panel door with repeated female figures and a lizard-shaped locking element, an architectural object plausibly made and used by the Dogon of Mali.

physical.title: door
physical.summary:
A carved wooden single leaf door with decoration (a-c) with a now separate piece which forms a lock (d); the two main pieces (a and b) almost rectangular once joined with large metal staples and an armature to form a two panel door; each
decorated in seven horizontal zones with rows of simplified standing female forms; the left hand panel is broken through near the top and a piece of it still connected to the right panel; stapled to the broken section an 'S'-shaped
seating for a large wooden bolt, in the form of a lizard's head and body; the right hand frame of the door, part of which (c) is now detached, extends five centimetres below the line and sixteen above to provide hinges; the wooden bolt (d) is a rectangular piece of wood tapering at one end, at its farther end a piece of the door jamb is still attached by a pivotal bent metal tack; much of the outer edges is now eaten away.
